TECHNOLOGY DELIVERY
AMIE SEISMIC MODELING COMES TO DAMMAM-7
The Geo- and Petrophysical Modeling and Instrumentation team in Moscow, in
collaboration with Geophysics Technology Division (GPD), has delivered the elastic
module of the Aramco Modeling and Inversion Engine (AMIE). The module performs
advanced seismic modeling using the spectral-element method, directly
incorporating the complex topography of the Earth's surface. It accurately simulates
how hills and valleys generate scattered reflections and diffractions within the
wavefield. This capability lies beyond the scope of modern commercial software. The
code is now available for testing with field data on Dammam-7 supercomputer. The
next step is to complete the acoustic modeling module by Q1/2026.

TECHNOLOGY MILESTONE
MRC's 2025 ADVANCEMENTS IN WATER MANAGEMENT
In 2025, the Advanced Materials Team in Moscow, in collaboration with the PTD and
RETD, achieved significant breakthroughs in advanced produced water treatment
aligned with a zero-liquid discharge goal. The team advanced three key technology-
approaches: Plasma Water Treatment, which uses energy-efficient in-water electric
discharges to degrade contaminants and reduce salinity; Surface-modified
Nanomembranes and ion-exchange resins “AzmPure”, which provide a robust
method of converting polymer waste into materials capable of effective water/oil
separation and desalination with demonstrated high efficiency; and bio-purification
BioPore, which leverages a pilot-scale bioreactor for the biodegradation of organic
contaminants. The next step is to upscale the processes and to work with EXPEC ARC
divisions for the deployment of the technologies by Q2/2026.

MRC's 2025 BREAKTHROUGH IN CRITICAL MINERALS EXPLORATION
Moscow Research Center, in collaboration with the GTD, GPD, and RETD, achieved
high outcomes in next-gen mineral exploration in 2025. In a major leap forward for
strategic resource development, the team has significantly advanced 5 flagship
projects. Three projects are aimed at software development: GEOMINE for geological,
geochemical, and satellite data analysis for sedimentary copper prospecting;
AquaMine for mineral detection in formation water; and GEMS for mineral

geophysical imaging. The other two projects are focused on process optimization:
SoLiEx - for lithium and associated strategic mineral recovery, soil desalination, and
water purification, and WasteLock - for reduction in the cost of extracting residual
minerals. The next step is to develop the innovative Lens-Ore project - a hybrid system
for instantly identifying minerals in core samples through a combination of chemical
processing and subsequent iLens imaging, without destroying the core by Q1/2026.

MRC's 2025 DIGITAL AND MODELLING PORTFOLIO EXECUTION AND KEY RESULTS
Moscow Research Center Team, in collaboration with the PTD, GTD, GPD, ATSD, DARC,
DTD, and RETD has delivered measurable progress across the digital and modelling
portfolio. Building on corporate TRV 2024 insights, where 76% of technologies were
digital, MRC realigned its focus to directly support the company’s operational
efficiency strategy. Key initiatives included expanding and maturing the digital and
modelling project pipeline, elevating existing solutions, and accelerating project
delivery. To address real operational challenges, MRC organized high-impact
workshops on Modelling and Digital Framework, engaging 15 leading Russian
technology partners. A dedicated booklet showcasing MRC digital capabilities was
also launched on TWIX, strengthening cross-division collaboration. As a result, 26% of
active technology projects were successfully completed and delivered in 2025, the
new project portfolio grew by 45%, and 85% of all work was executed in-house.
Looking ahead, the new digital and modelling strategy focuses on scaling projects
with proven value and establishing a continuous, high-quality idea pipeline for 2026.

UPSCALING COOPERATION AND PROGRESS BETWEEN MRC AND EXPEC ARC

Development Group member Rafael M. Pino to Moscow Research Center in January

MRC's 2025 PROGRESS IN OPERATIONAL GEOSCIENCE SOLUTIONS
The Geo- and Petrophysical Modeling and Instrumentation (GPMI) Team in Moscow,
in collaboration with GPD, GTD, and DTD, enhanced its core modeling and
engineering capabilities to deliver advanced, field-ready solutions aligned with
Aramco’s operational priorities. This focused capability development led to seven

borehole and VSP interpretation; GEMS, developing electromagnetic geophysics
solutions for geohazard assessment and mineral exploration; and GeoRover, an
autonomous robotic platform for seismic acquisition. The next phase emphasizes
operational testing and technology maturation in 2026.

LAB UPSCALING: PRODUCED WATER TREATMENT FROM RESIDUAL
HYDROCARBON REMOVAL
The Advanced Materials Team in Moscow, in collaboration with the Production
Technology Division (PTD), has successfully assembled an upscaled 100-L flow-
through prototype purification unit for produced water treatment. The system
integrates selective microorganisms integrated into the advanced sorbent materials
to continuously remove residual hydrocarbons. First results show hydrocarbon
concentration drop from 2000 ppm to below 10 ppm during the purification cycle. The

next step will focus on completing the system testing by Q2/2025.

TECHNOLOGY RE-BRANDING CHALLENGE: FROM TECHNICAL TITLES TO
RECOGNIZABLE BRANDS
Moscow Research Center delivered the Technology Re-Branding Challenge,
converting complex technology names into clear, memorable, and management-
ready brands. In total, 30 technologies were covered, generating more than 500
naming ideas that were refined through a structured selection process. The resulting
brand names combined two complementary naming directions, spanning English
descriptive and concept-driven titles such as DryWell, AcidSim, SeismoSmart, Sonic-
Vision, Earth Vibes, SafeDrill, SealFlex, NanoFrac, Cavity Sense, and WaterBullFort,
alongside Arabic-inspired names including MEEZAN.AI (نازيم), MAJD (د  جْ
م), NASR (رصن),
DALIL (ليلد), and DIFA (عافد), presented in English transliteration and aligned with the
core meaning of each project. The challenge established a clear and consistent
foundation for technology branding. The approved brand names will be integrated
into official materials and daily communication by Q1/2026.

DELIVERED TECHONOLOGY
ASAD SWARM CONTROL STATION
The Geo- and Petrophysical Modeling & Instrumentation Team in Moscow, in
collaboration with Geophysics Technology Division (GPD), have delivered the Swarm
Control Station (SCS) in Dhahran. The SCS is a stationary, fully integrated control setup
incorporating a single-board computer, industrial Wi-Fi router, RTK GNSS, and LoRa
communication modules with high-power antennas. A new autonomous power
solution based on a high-capacity battery and solar panels is implemented, ensuring
full energy self-sufficiency of the system. During field tests, the SCS demonstrated
stable and robust communication, enabling coordinated operation of a hybrid ASAD
swarm comprising multiple drone generations, including ASAD 2.0. Next is to upscale
the SCS and install it in ASAD mobile recorder by Q4/2026.

FROM SATELLITE TO ALGORITHM: SAUDI ARABIA'S COPPER EXPLORATION
The Advanced Materials Team in Moscow, in collaboration with the Geology
Technology Division (GTD), has created the in-house collection of geological maps,
maps of geophysical fields, geochemical data, multispectral satellite images of Saudi
Arabia, and reference data on the world's copper deposits. This systematized
database is essential for forecasting copper deposits in arid environments. The
developing technology significantly reduces the time and costs of geological
exploration by enabling targeted identification of prospective areas. The next step will
be development and training of machine learning algorithms using the compiled data
collection and verifying the approach for the testing location by Q2/2026.

TECHNOLOGY MILESTONE
A SOFTWARE PROTOTYPE FOR CARBON DIOXIDE WELLBORE FLOW SIMULATION
The Advanced Materials Team in Moscow, in collaboration with the Reservoir
Engineering Technology Division, has developed a model to simulate the process of
simultaneous injection of water and carbon dioxide nanobubbles through the well to
the reservoir. The model is based on the numerical solution of partial differential
equations describing multiphase gas-liquid flow and realized as a Python software
prototype. It enables prediction of the multiphase flow regime at downhole
conditions by using a model-based approach for nano- and microbubble transport.
The developed tool also facilitates the solution to the broad range of applied
problems, which include optimization of CO2 sequestration, wastewater treatment,

improving oil production, drilling fluids density, and injection control. It can be
adapted as well to enhance mineral extraction and processing. The next step is to
validate the workflow with real data in Q1/2026.

PREDICTOR OF FLUID PROPERTIES FOR PLANNING CO2 SEQUESTRATION IN DEEP
SALINE AQUIFERS
The Advanced Materials team in Moscow, in collaboration with the Reservoir
Engineering Technology Division (RETD), have developed a predictor of vapor-liquid
equilibria in deep saline aquifers rich with H2S. The model predicts the amount of CO2
that can be injected at given pressure. It constitutes a necessary step towards
reservoir scale planning of CCUS efforts and will help reducing laborious
experimentation with high-pressure H2S. Expansion of capabilities and user interface
development is planned to finish in Q2/2026.

ITQAN PROJECT KICK-OFF: 1st DRILLING FLUIDS DIGITAL PLANNING, CONTROL,

The Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics Team in Moscow, in collaboration with
ATSD, has initiated ITQAN. The project will be devoted to creating the first software

optimization using offset-well intelligence. The technology is expected to reduce NPT
and fluids-related risks, improve operational safety, and lower overall fluids cost
through better material utilization planning and tighter execution control. The next
step is development of the drilling fluid composition formulator by Q2/2026.

DELIVERED TECHONOLOGY
THE ATHAR-METALS SURVEY: DELIVERING A ROADMAP FOR OIL EXPLORATION
The Advanced Materials Team in Moscow, in collaboration with the Geology
Technology Division (GTD) has performed a comprehensive geochemical survey that
has identified prospective oil fields based on the characteristic inorganic indicators.
The analysis of loosely bound metals - specifically Ti, V, Ni, and Cu in 336 soil samples
from 8 oil fields for direct detection of hydrocarbon accumulation has been
successfully completed. The key deliverables include the complete geochemical
dataset, visualization reports, SOPs, and a preliminary interpretation. The next step
will be to integrate ATHAR-Metals project data with organic indicators from ATHAR-
Hydrocarbon project to improve the accuracy of oilfield prediction by Q2/2026.

NEW PROJECT INITIATION: PHYSICS-INFORMED AI FOR FRACTURE PLACEMENT
OPTIMIZATION
The Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics Team in Moscow, in collaboration with
the Reservoir Engineering Technology Division (RETD), has launched a project to
automate preliminary hydraulic-fracturing design for tight gas reservoirs. The
objective is to develop an algorithm that combines AI capabilities, well log data, and
physics-based constraints to provide engineers with fracture geometry and optimal
placement. This workflow will streamline the internal screening process before
submitting final locations to a service company for detailed design, reducing the time
and cost associated with suboptimal fracturing strategies. The next step is to validate
the approach and test it on real data by Q3/2026.

approved internal sources, and strengthened anti-spam controls and monitoring.

removed the block and restored service access. To further enhance security and
ensure full compliance with Saudi Aramco cybersecurity requirements, a migration to
the Softline Cloud Email Solution with a dedicated deployment is underway, with full
transition targeted by Q2/2026.

NASR TECHNOLOGY ACHIEVES FIRST SUBSURFACE IMAGE
The Geo- and Petrophysical Instrumentation Team in Moscow, in collaboration with
Geophysics Technology Division (GPD), successfully implemented an advanced
geological model imaging algorithm, establishing NASR. The solution achieves 4-
meter resolution, proven on models with shallow seabed structures and caves. This
precise subsurface visualization technology is a critical tool for preventing drilling
hazards in cave-prone areas. Next step is to test the technology and build the
geological model imaging using Aramco data in Q1/ 2026.

NEXT PHASE OF SAUDI ARAMCO FIBER OPTIC SOFTWARE (SAFOS) DEVELOPMENT
The Geo- and Petrophysical Instrumentation Team in Moscow, in collaboration with
the Production Technology Division (PTD), prepares for the development of v3.0 of
SAFOS software. Previous version implemented injectivity profile measurement based
on distributed temperature sensing (DTS) data and optimized the legacy code base.
The new version is targeted to bring new interpretative features such as distributed
temperature sensing (DTS) leak detection, to modernize the software technology
stack to improve the performance and to comply with the company software
development guidelines. Proposed technology stack was discussed with UDC. The
project alignment with the business needs was confirmed with the field proponents.
The business value of new version will be in improving well integrity control,
shortening turnaround time for the interpretation and simplified deployment to the
field proponents. The next step is to develop physics based DTS leak detection work
flow and to develop SAFOS v3.0 architecture based on modern technology stack by
Q4/2026.

FALCONEYE: INITIAL AI-BASED MUD WEIGHT PREDICTION FOR HITH FORMATION
The Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics Team in Moscow, in collaboration with
the Drilling Technology Division (DTD), has developed and validated a first baseline
mud-weight prediction model for the Hith Formation in the Jafurah Basin. The model
uses a CNN-based transfer-learning approach trained on intrinsic structural-geometry
features, leveraging a pre-trained FalconEye model from the JILH Formation (Ghawar
Field). The model was fine-tuned and validated using a limited well dataset of 42 wells,
achieving an initial prediction accuracy of 80%. Next step includes joint engagement
with field proponents in Q1/2026 to refine the dataset and improve prediction

accuracy to 90-95% - comparable to the performance achieved on the JILH Formation.

FROM BRINE TO MINE: SoLiEx MINERALS EXTRACTION APPROACH
The Advanced Materials Team in Moscow, in collaboration with the Geology
Technology Division (GTD), has successfully demonstrated the potential of SoLiEx
technique (2022 Ebtikar finalist project), for selective extraction of minerals in
aqueous solutions. By washing Sabkha saline soils, the sequence of salt cation
leaching during desalination was determined. This experimental discovery facilitates
the optimization of mineral separation and allows for the regulation of the amount of
water required during the washing, a key factor in the efficient extraction of minerals
from soils. The next step will be to experimentally determine the relationship between
the required volume of water and key soil parameters: the amount of soil processed,
its particle size distribution, and salinity level by Q1/2026.

PRODUCTION FLUIDS ENHANCED BY NANOPARTICLES
The Advanced Materials Team in Moscow, in collaboration with the Production
Technology Division (PTD), has completed the characterization of nanomaterials and
testing their rheological performance in production fluids, marking a key milestone in
the NanoFrac project. According to the results obtained, nanoparticle loading (up to
0.5%) in fluids gives significant boost to viscosity, which would allow guar gum loading
to be reduced by up to 25%. The next step is to create and test fluids with
nanoparticles using a wide range of additives to improve performance under high
temperatures, pressures, and salinities by Q2/2026.

NO-CODE PLATFORM FOR AUTOMATED VISUAL ANALYSIS OF ROCK IMAGES
The Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics Team in Moscow, in collaboration with
the Digital ARC, has successfully built the foundation for a no-code platform to analyze
geological images. Drill core and thin section images for over 5,000 wells have been
collected from open-source repositories. The machine learning framework and
methodology have been finalized to predict lithology and other properties. Mockups
and a roadmap have been created to guide platform development. The next phase
focusing on training neural network models and developing the ML workflow will be
completed in Q2/2026.

TECHONOLOGY MILESTONE
LOW POWER PLASMA TOOL ACHIEVES FULL DESTRUCTION OF FIELD CARBONATE
SCALE
The Advanced Materials Team in Moscow, in collaboration with Production
Technology Division (PTD), has successfully validated a novel portable low power
plasma tool for scale removal, achieving complete significant destruction of 6 cm-
deep carbonate scale from KSA field sample. The technology’s dual-action mechanism
—using shockwaves to fracture the scale while chemically active species dissolve the
particles—offers a significant leap in operational efficiency compared to traditional
chemical treatments, which would require substantial volumes and extended
intervention time for the same severity of scale. The results indicate that this
technology would offer the possibility for lowering operational costs and minimizing
non-productive time. Next is to test the removal of sulfate scale samples as well as the
energy efficiency and operational costs estimation by Q2/2026.

SAUDI COPPER PRODUCTION: NEW SUBSURFACE LEACHING TECH

copper leaching and recovery. The method is expected to dramatically boost copper
leaching from scattered ores based on the proprietary chemicals pumped downhole.
The team has secured direct ties with both the industrial and scientific developers,
who are ready to tailor the process to the Saudi Arabia ore conditions. The next step is

A NEW PROJECT INITIATION FOR PREDICTIVE TUBING IRON SULFIDE SCALE
CONTROL IN GAS WELLS
The Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics Team in Moscow, in collaboration with
the Production Technology Division (PTD), have launched a data-driven tubing scale
management framework for gas wells. The project aims to integrate geochemical,
thermodynamic, and production data with advanced AI/ML models to forecast tubing
scale deposition, reduce formation risk, minimize downtime, and optimize preventive
and chemical removal strategies. The next phase will validate the framework using
real field data, with testing targeted for Q3/2026.
